## Today's Goals {.smaller}

Today we will

- More Modeling
  - Generating Predictions
  - Visually Evaluating Models
- Modeling in R
  - Implement a univariate linear model in R

We will use the CRU **and** FAO data

- `AGNR-AREC280_Fall2026/Data/CRU/parquet`
  - Filter to annual data
- `AGNR-AREC280_Fall2026/Data/FAO/parquet`
  - Filter to Avocado Yields
- Join on `Year` and `ISO3` into a single dataset




  
## Loading Datasets

First load the CRU and FAO data from Parquet Files

```{r load_fao}
#| echo: true
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
# Load the full fao dataset
read_parquet(
  file.path(data_path,"FAO","parquet","FAO_crop_livestock.parquet")
) |>
  filter(Item == "Avocados" & Element == "Yield") -> faostat_avocado

read_parquet(
  file.path(data_path,"CRU","parquet","tmp_w_ISO3.parquet")
) |>
  filter(Period == "ANN") -> cru_tmp_ann

faostat_avocado |>
  inner_join(cru_tmp_ann,join_by(ISO3,Year),suffix=c("_fao","_cru")) |>
  drop_na(ISO3) -> avocado_tmp
```

# Recap from last class 

## Modeling a single country

The country seems to matter a lot for yields

- We'll think about how to model country effects later
- Let's start off focusing on only Mexico
```{r filter-mexico}
#| echo: true
avocado_tmp |>
  filter(ISO3 == "MEX") -> avocado_tmp_mex
```



## Training an OLS Model

Train the following OLS model on the Mexico Avocado Yield data
$$Yield = b_0 + b_1 Temperature + \epsilon$$

```{r train-ols}
#| echo: true
lm(
  Value_fao ~ Value_cru,
  data=avocado_tmp_mex
) -> yield_model

print(yield_model)
```
What does this mean?
```{r extract-params}
b0 = coefficients(yield_model)[["(Intercept)"]]
b1 = coefficients(yield_model)[["Value_cru"]]
pred_fn <- function(x) b0 + b1 * x
```



## Visualizing Our Model

```{r yield-plot-4}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
ggplot(data=avocado_tmp_mex,aes(x=Value_cru,y=Value_fao)) +
  geom_point(aes(color=Year),size=3) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept=coefficients(yield_model)[["(Intercept)"]],
    slope=coefficients(yield_model)[["Value_cru"]],
    color="red",linewidth=1.2
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x="Annual Average Temperature (C)",
    y="Yeild (mt/ha)",
    title="Avocado Yeilds in Mexico"
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c()
```


# Formatting Output

## Using `moderndive`

```{r show-reg-table}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
library(moderndive)
get_regression_table(yield_model)
```

## Formatting table output

```{r show-reg-table-kable}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
library(knitr)
get_regression_table(yield_model) |> 
  kable(format="html")
```

## Using `moderndive` {.smaller}

```{r get-predictions}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
get_regression_points(yield_model) -> yield_model_points
print(yield_model_points)
```


## Evaluating Model Predictions

```{r eval-predictions-viz}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
ggplot(yield_model_points) +
  geom_point(aes(x=Value_fao,y=Value_fao_hat),color="black",size=1.5) +
  geom_abline(slope=1,intercept=0,color="red",linewidth=1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title="Modeled Yields for Mexico",
    x="Actual Yield",
    y="Predicted Yield"
  )
```

## Applying the Model

```{r subset-columbia}
#| echo: true
avocado_tmp |>
  filter(ISO3 == "COL") -> avocado_tmp_col
```

## Use model to predict

```{r predict-col}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
get_regression_points(yield_model,newdata=avocado_tmp_col) -> forecast_col
print(forecast_col)
```

## Visualize Predictions
```{r eval-predictions-viz-col}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
ggplot(forecast_col) +
  geom_point(aes(x=Value_fao,y=Value_fao_hat),color="black",size=1.5) +
  geom_abline(slope=1,intercept=0,color="red",linewidth=1) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title="Modeled Yields for Columbia",
    x="Actual Yield",
    y="Predicted Yield"
  )
```
